author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield eased Friday after moving close to 5%, giving global bond markets a pause from a sharp selloff. Reuters reported the benchmark yield near 4.93% at the cited close, down about one basis point on the session. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

August consumer-price data largely matched expectations, with prices rising 0.4% from July and 3.4% from a year earlier. The report reduced the immediate pressure for an even more abrupt repricing, but it did not remove concern that elevated energy costs could keep inflation persistent. Traders have increased attention on the possibility of higher policy rates, while some policymakers may prefer to wait for additional data.

The 5% level matters because Treasury yields influence borrowing costs across mortgages, corporate debt and asset valuations. Earlier market stress also followed an unsuccessful Treasury buyback operation, adding to questions about demand at current prices. Friday's retreat was modest and does not establish a trend; it records where the market stood at the Reuters timestamp after an unusually volatile week for government bonds.
dek: A global bond selloff paused Friday after U.S. inflation data matched forecasts, leaving the benchmark yield near 4.93% at the cited close.
headline: U.S. 10-year Treasury yield retreats from 5% threshold
